milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining white carpet causes it to drop as an item that the player automatically picks up into inventory. White carpet breaks instantly with bare hands and always drops itself. The player starts with an empty inventory (verified in sandbox), so having at least 1 white_carpet in inventory conclusively proves the player mined it. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks per the mapping guidelines.

scene_description: A small oak plank room (7x5 exterior) with a stone brick floor, white carpet covering the interior floor (5x3 = 15 blocks), glowstone ceiling light, and a 2-block-high doorway facing the player's spawn. The surrounding area is cleared of trees to ensure clear navigation. Player spawns ~4 blocks from the doorway on a stone brick path.
task_text: Enter the wooden room ahead and mine white carpet from the floor.
design_notes: The room is offset ~4 blocks forward (positive Z) from player spawn. The first command clears a large area of trees/leaves to prevent navigation obstacles. Grass block floor is placed, then stone bricks for the room foundation and approach path. The room has oak plank walls (3 blocks high), a solid oak plank roof, and a 2-block-high doorway at the center of the front wall (Z=4). White carpet fills the interior floor (5x3 grid from ~-2,~0,~5 to ~2,~0,~7). Glowstone in the ceiling provides lighting. Player needs to walk forward ~4 blocks, enter the doorway, look down, and attack the white carpet to mine it.
